sentences.text: Revenue compounded 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201], but the path was cyclical rather than smooth.
The window opened with a 18.0% rebound in FY2017 [D42] and a 20.4% jump in FY2018 [D92], then fell 22.4% in FY2020 [D198] before recovering 22.1% in FY2021 [D251].
The FY2020 decline came from lower sales volume driven by lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].
FY2023 was the margin peak, with operating profit up 64.0% [D358] on favorable price realization, higher sales volume and the absence of a 2022 goodwill impairment [P31].
North America carried the latest year, contributing 3.4pp of the 4.3% revenue growth [D515][D463] and reaching 54.2% of revenue [D513].
North America sales rose 6% on higher sales volume, mainly higher sales of equipment to end users, partly offset by unfavorable price realization [P12].
Power & Energy grew 11.6% and contributed 5.2pp [D758][D759], while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D765][D766].
Construction Industries' decline was primarily unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher sales volume of $568 million [P8].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, a 28.6% CAGR against 6.4% [F202][F201], but in FY2025 it fell 14.7% against revenue growth of 4.3% [D464][D463].
Operating margin was 16.5% in FY2025 [F30], above the 14.3% window median [D1123] but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [D1122].
The 3.7pp decline in FY2025 [D476] came almost entirely from cost of revenue, which added 4.2pp of margin pressure [D490] as it rose to 66.2% of revenue [D441].

Operating profit fell primarily on unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion and unfavorable price realization of $817 million, with manufacturing costs largely reflecting higher tariffs [P9].
Net margin fell 3.5pp to 13.1% [D477][F50], tracking the operating decline, with the 24.0% effective tax rate [D449] leaving net margin 3.4pp below operating margin [D1168].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion [F80] was 1.32x net income [D450], above the 1.16x window median [D1158], while free cash flow of $8.9 billion [F100] was 1.00x net income [D451].
Free cash flow margin was 13.2% [D447], above the 11.9% window median [D1129] but below the 16.8% FY2023 high [D1128].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes, partly offset by lower profit [P4].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.821 billion [D470][F90], lifting capex to 4.2% of revenue [D446] and capex/D&A to 1.25x [D452], the highest in the window.
Cash rose 44.9% to $9.980 billion [D472][F140] while total debt grew 14.1% to $36.210 billion [D485][D455], leaving net debt of $26.230 billion [D456].

Net debt was 38.8% of revenue [D457], a smaller net debt burden than the peer median of -59.4% net cash and in the 67th percentile of three peers [D1170][D1169], though the pack omits long-term debt due within one year [R7].
Buybacks and dividends of $7.939 billion [D458] were 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Return on average equity was 43.5% [D462], in the 100th percentile of six industrials peers against a 23.3% median [D1155][D1156].
Total debt and net cash omit long-term debt due within one year, which the filer reports at $7.1 billion in FY2025 [R7][X180][D455], so leverage is understated.
Net debt rose for a second year through FY2025 [R1][D350][D403][D456], and the omitted current maturities make the true level higher still.
Revenue declined 3.4% in FY2024 [R2][D410] on lower sales volume, partly offset by favorable price realization [P22].
Net income for FY2021-FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy statement rather than the 10-K, differing by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20].
Operating margin: a FY2026 reading below the 14.3% window median [D1123] would confirm the tariff-driven cost pressure described for FY2025 [P9], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Capex: a ratio above the FY2025 1.25x capex/D&A [D452] would extend the capital-intensity climb and pressure free cash flow margin below the 13.2% latest level [D447].
Construction Industries: a return to growth after the FY2025 1.6% decline [D765] would reverse the segment drag, with first-quarter 2026 guidance pointing to strong sales growth [P15].
